# Getting started with Microsoft Copilot in everyday apps

By the end of this guide, you'll know where Microsoft Copilot lives on your Windows PC, how to bring it up, and you'll have completed a useful first task. Imagine turning a rough email into a tidy summary, or getting a quick overview of a long web page – that's what Copilot helps you do. This tutorial is for anyone who wants a quicker, smarter way to work, whether you're handling personal errands or day-to-day office duties.

## Before you start
-   You have a Windows PC with a working internet connection (the Copilot app comes preinstalled on new Windows 11 PCs).
-   You are signed in with a Microsoft account (the same one you use for Windows, Outlook, or Office).
-   Your built-in apps – Microsoft Edge, Outlook, Word, PowerPoint – are up to date (they usually update automatically in the background).
-   Some features, especially within Office apps like Word, Outlook, or PowerPoint, require a Microsoft 365 plan that includes Copilot. Microsoft has also changed its plan names over time, so check your account page to see what yours includes. This guide focuses on features that are easy to reach.
-   Rough total time: This guide should take you about 5-10 minutes to follow along with.

## Step 1 — Spot the Copilot icon
The Copilot icon acts like a little helper button in Microsoft Edge. To begin, open Microsoft Edge, your internet browser. Look at the upper-right corner of the browser window.

**What you see on screen:** You'll typically see several small icons. Look for the Copilot icon. Its look can change between Edge versions, so if you are unsure, point at an icon for a moment and read its label.
**What happens next:** Nothing happens yet when you just spot it; you're just identifying your starting point.
**If it looks different:** If you don't see it there, update Edge and check again. The exact place and design of the icon can differ between versions.
💬 Example: (No typing needed for this step, just observation.)
**You'll know it worked when:** You can clearly see the Copilot icon in your Microsoft Edge browser window.

## Step 2 — Open Copilot in Microsoft Edge
Once you've spotted the Copilot icon in Microsoft Edge, it's time to activate it. Click on that button. This action is like tapping a friend on the shoulder to get their attention.

**What you see on screen:** After clicking, Copilot opens next to the page you are viewing. This is where you'll chat with Copilot.
**What happens next:** The Copilot panel appears with a box for typing your request. This means it's ready for your instructions.
**If it looks different:** The exact layout can differ between Edge versions. If the icon isn't there, make sure your Edge browser is up to date and that you are signed in with your Microsoft account.
💬 Example: `Summarize this article about recent climate change research.`
**You'll know it worked when:** The Copilot panel is open in your Edge browser, and you see a text input area ready for your question or command. Copilot can use the context of the page you have open, and depending on your settings it may also use other open tabs. You can review or change this in Edge's settings under Copilot and AI, so it only sees what you are comfortable sharing.

## Step 3 — Use Copilot in Outlook to tidy an email
Microsoft Copilot can help you quickly understand lengthy emails, saving you time. First, open your Microsoft Outlook application and select an email that has a good amount of text or information.

**What you see on screen:** With a longer email conversation open, Outlook can offer a summary from Copilot at the top of the conversation, where you may see a "Summary by Copilot" or "Summarize" option. The exact appearance varies between Outlook versions and plans.
**What happens next:** Selecting that option shows a short summary of the conversation. If you have a Copilot chat or panel in Outlook, you can also type your own instruction there.
**If it looks different:** If you can't find any Copilot option, your Outlook version or Microsoft 365 plan may not include it yet. Copilot features in Office apps depend on your plan and on updates. Check your plan details in your Microsoft account.
💬 Example: `Summarize this email in three bullet points, focusing on key action items.`
**You'll know it worked when:** Copilot displays a concise summary of the email, often presented as bullet points, based on your instruction. Copilot can draft the summary, but you stay in charge of sending any message, and it can miss highly nuanced human emotion or sarcasm.

## Step 4 — Generate a slide outline in PowerPoint
Getting started with a presentation can be daunting, but Copilot can help you create a structure. Open Microsoft PowerPoint and start a new, blank presentation. This gives Copilot a clean slate to work with.

**What you see on screen:** Look for Copilot among the options at the top of the PowerPoint window. The top area with all your editing options is called the "ribbon". The exact label and position of the Copilot option can differ between versions.
**What happens next:** Selecting it opens a Copilot panel or a box where you can type your request for the presentation outline.
**If it looks different:** If you can't find Copilot in PowerPoint, your PowerPoint version or Microsoft 365 plan may not include it yet. Copilot in Office apps depends on your plan and on app updates.
💬 Example: `Create an outline for a 5-slide presentation on how to reduce household energy consumption.`
**You'll know it worked when:** Copilot generates a list of slide titles and perhaps some key talking points. Copilot provides a structure, but it can't replace your own judgment, so review the content for accuracy before you use it.

## Step 5 — Open the Copilot app in Windows
Copilot is also available as its own app on Windows, which is handy when you want a quick answer without opening a browser.

**What you see on screen:** Look for the Copilot app in the taskbar or in the Start menu. Some keyboards have a Copilot key, and on many Windows 11 PCs you can also press the Windows key + C to open it. Which of these work depends on your PC and Windows updates.
**What happens next:** The Copilot app opens with a box for typing your question. You may be asked to sign in with your Microsoft account.
**If it looks different:** If you can't find it, search for "Copilot" from the Start menu. If it isn't installed, you can usually get it from the Microsoft Store.
💬 Example: `What is the current time in London, UK?`
**You'll know it worked when:** The Copilot app opens, and after you type your question and press Enter, Copilot shows an answer. For important facts, double-check the answer with an official source.

## Common mistakes
-   **Looking in the wrong place:** Copilot shows up in different places in different apps and versions. If you can't find it, check that the app is up to date and that your account or plan includes Copilot.
-   **Leaving the query too vague:** Simply typing "Help me" often leads to broad or unhelpful answers. Instead, provide clear, specific instructions. For example, rather than "Summarize this," try "Summarize this email in three bullet points, highlighting the deadlines."
-   **Forgetting to sign in:** Copilot relies on your Microsoft account to access certain features and integrate with your documents securely. If you see a sign-in prompt, follow the steps to log in before proceeding. Without being signed in, many Copilot features will be unavailable or limited.

## What this means for you
-   **In everyday life:** You can quickly turn a lengthy email about a community event into a short checklist, or get the gist of a long news article in seconds, freeing up time for other activities.
-   **For your business or work:** Generate meeting-ready PowerPoint outlines in minutes, or summarize dense project documents, allowing you to focus on strategic thinking rather than administrative tasks.
-   **If you're just getting started:** The easiest first move is to open Microsoft Edge, navigate to any interesting article, then open Copilot in the side panel and ask it to summarize the page.

## Try it now
Open Microsoft Edge, browse to any news website you like, then click the Copilot icon in the upper-right corner. In the text box that appears, type `Summarize the main article on this homepage in two short sentences.` In the next two minutes, you'll see how Copilot quickly pulls the main ideas together – giving you a practical taste of how it can help you across all your everyday apps.
